main_text.p: cuentu ? hercle infausto, & tanta digno audacia. {1} Genfericus enim Vandolorum Rex, rogatu Eudoxiæ Imperatricis, ingenti Classe in Italiam adnauigans, Romam nullo aduersante facilè ingreditur, Maximum è vestigio Romani fugientem infectati, lapidibus obruunt, membratimque discerpunt. Ita Maximum insequuta est vltio diuina, quòd in Imperatorè violentas manus iniicere non formidauerit, licèt in suo & vxoris nomine ab infamia vindicdo[?], & turpissimo facinore vlcifcendo, Regicidarũ patronis iustissimè factû videatur: Imò, nõ solũ inmorte, sed & in vitâ post hoc facinus admissu & imperium adeptum, irę Cœlestis pondus sentiebat.] Cũ enim omnibus viribus ad principalis apicis abruptum ventum esset (inquit, m Lib.2.epist.13.{m}Sidonius) quandam potestatis immensæ vertiginem, sub coronâ patiebatur, nec sustinebat Dominus esse, qui non sustinuerat esse sub domino.] Non ita multò post, ad Imperium Orientale succef-fit Anastasius, qui in Eutychetis & Dioscori lapsis Hȩrefin,multa Orthodoxis Ecclesijs detrimenta intulit,omnibus-

page.notes: Left margin notes: "1 Idam ibi-dem." (mark 1 keyed to "Genfericus" in the text) and "m Lib.2.epist.13." (mark m keyed to "Sidonius" in the text). The marks are shown as {1} and {m} in the text; the note element carries only the m mark, the note for mark 1 is written as printed above. The right page is cut off at the scan edge. Its visible line beginnings are transcribed as fragments only, and the line order is uncertain. The original letters are shown in the fragment paragraph. Doubtful readings: "vindicdo" (possibly a printing error for "vindicado"); "cuentu ?" is the fragment of a word at the top of the page; "Hȩrefin" is as printed. The bracket marks [ and ] appear in the text as printed and are not editorial additions.
